findings.title: Merged PR comment helpers are attached to the wrong class
findings.body: `_truncate_title`, `get_environment_info`, and `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` were added to `CommitContextIntegration`, but the GitHub and GitLab workflows call them on `PRCommentWorkflow` instances. Those workflow instances do not expose these methods, so generating a merged PR/MR comment raises `AttributeError` before it can be posted. Additionally, this method invokes `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title` even though the helper was declared on `CommitContextIntegration`. Move the helpers to `PRCommentWorkflow` or call them through the workflow's integration object consistently.

findings.title: Feature-gated dashboard tables discard the query result
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the table path renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and a hard-coded empty `tableData` object instead of `fields`, `result.data`, and `result.meta`. Consequently every dashboard table widget for an enabled organization has no headers or rows, and it also bypasses the existing loading and error behavior. Adapt and pass the actual table result to the new visualization before enabling this path.

findings.title: Attribute-key query cache key is not scoped to the organization
findings.body: The new React Query key contains only `queryOptions`, while the query function fetches from an organization-specific URL. In particular, with no selected projects, switching organizations with the same date range and attribute type reuses the same cache key, so attributes from the previously selected organization can be displayed (and may not be refetched). Include `organization.slug` or the full endpoint path in `queryKey`.

findings.title: Zero-valued age and timestamp bypass mutual-exclusion validation
findings.body: The validators use `self.initial_data.get(...)` to test whether the other field was supplied. JSON reports containing both `age: 0` and `timestamp: 0` therefore pass both checks because zero is falsy, despite the endpoint requiring the two report formats to be mutually exclusive. Test field presence (for example, `'age' in self.initial_data`) rather than truthiness in both validators.

findings.title: Falsy custom cell render results incorrectly fall back to the default renderer
findings.body: Both default renderer wrappers use `if (cell)` even though the renderer contract says only `undefined` should request fallback and `React.ReactNode` validly includes `0`, `false`, an empty string, and `null`. A custom body renderer cannot intentionally render a blank cell or a numeric zero; the default field renderer is used instead. Check `cell !== undefined` in both the head and body renderer paths.
